name: PCF8574 I2C I/O Expander
summary: Eight more pins over two wires, and the chip on every I2C LCD backpack. Quasi-bidirectional outputs, which is the catch.
notes: There are no registers. You write one byte and you read one byte, which makes it trivial to drive and impossible to configure.
Outputs are quasi-bidirectional: a strong pull-down but only a weak 100 uA pull-up. They sink 25 mA happily and source almost nothing, so wire LEDs to the positive rail and sink through the pin.
To use a pin as an input, write a 1 to it first. That releases it to the weak pull-up, and an external switch to ground then reads as 0. Writing a 0 and then reading gives you 0 forever.
A0, A1 and A2 set the low three address bits: 0x20 to 0x27 on the PCF8574, and 0x38 to 0x3F on the PCF8574A. Sellers mix the two parts freely, so scan the bus before assuming.
INT (pin 13) is open drain and pulses on any input change, which saves polling. It needs its own pull-up.
If you need real configurable pull-ups, push-pull outputs or per-pin direction, the MCP23017 does all three for a little more money and a register map.

pins.name: A0
pins.note: Tie high or low. Never leave floating.

pins.name: P0
pins.note: Sinks 25 mA, sources 100 uA. Wire loads to the positive rail.

pins.name: INT
pins.note: Pulses low on any input change. Needs a pull-up.

pins.name: VDD
pins.note: 100 nF to ground at the pin.

snippets.title: Read and write the port over I2C
snippets.gotcha: There are no registers and no direction bits. Writing 1 releases a pin to a weak 100 uA pull-up so it can be read; writing 0 pulls it hard low. Outputs sink 25 mA but barely source, so wire LEDs to the positive rail.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit

parts.why: I2C data is open drain and there are no internal pull-ups on the bus.
The matching pull-up for the clock line.
Address bit 0. These three pins set the I2C address and must not be left floating.
Address bit 1. All three low gives 0x20 on the PCF8574, 0x38 on the PCF8574A.
Address bit 2. Eight devices fit on one bus, which is the point of the part.
INT is open drain too. Only needed if you use the change interrupt.

circuit.note: The outputs are quasi-bidirectional: they can only sink 25 mA and source about 100 uA. Drive LEDs to ground, not from the pin, and write a 1 to a pin before using it as an input.
